title: AMG Lithium opens test laboratory for solid electrolytes in Frankfurt - electrive.com
content:
AMG Lithium has commissioned its new Performance Lab "PerLa" in Frankfurt, Germany. The company aims to test sulfide solid electrolytes under more realistic conditions in complete laboratory cells and further develop them with customers.
AMG Lithium's laboratory in Frankfurt for solid electrolytes.
Image: AMG Lithium
AMG Lithium
is expanding its development activities for solid-state batteries with a new laboratory at its Frankfurt site. The laboratory space is increasing by 250 to around 1,100 square metres. The centrepiece is a glovebox line that can replicate the entire manufacturing process of laboratory cells under controlled, inert atmospheric conditions.
This includes the production of electrode pastes, coating, cell assembly and, finally, packaging as pouch cells. The company says more than 200 test stations are available for electrochemical investigations.
The real advancement, however, lies less in the additional laboratory space and more in the ability to test its own materials under application-relevant conditions. AMG Lithium can now not only characterise its solid electrolytes at the material level but also examine them in complete battery cells using standardised test protocols.
This is intended to facilitate joint development projects with customers in particular. AMG Lithium is thus positioning itself more strongly at the interface between material development and cell validation, although this does not include industrial cell production.
The new Glovebox-Linie enables the production of complete laboratory cells under inert atmosphere.
Focus on sulphide solid electrolytes
AMG Lithium is developing sulphide solid electrolytes for future solid-state batteries in Frankfurt. Such materials are intended to replace the liquid electrolytes in today’s lithium-ion cells. The technology fundamentally promises advantages in energy density and safety but continues to face challenges in material stability, cell integration and industrial manufacturing.
This is precisely why validation in complete cells is crucial. Material properties that can be demonstrated well on a laboratory scale must also prove themselves in interaction with electrodes, interfaces and real-world manufacturing processes.
With PerLa, AMG Lithium now aims to represent this step more strongly in-house. The company describes this step as an important building block for the market entry of its solid electrolyte technology. However, AMG Lithium has not yet provided specific details about its customer projects, offtake agreements or a potential production ramp-up for solid electrolytes.
In parallel, the company is expanding its industrial base for battery materials in Germany. In Bitterfeld-Wolfen, AMG Lithium is increasing its capacity for producing battery-grade lithium salts. For this undertaking, the company has been granted €36 million from the German federal funding initiative
as part of a total investment of €180 million. The plan is to achieve an annual capacity of 20,000 tonnes of battery-grade lithium compounds at the facility. According to the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, this theoretically corresponds to battery production of around 34 GWh per year.

title: Ecobat break-up complete as Clarios acquires North American recycling business – Batteries International
content: Clarios is set to acquire Ecobat’s remaining lead recycling operations in the US, just weeks after Ecobat exited its lithium recycling business to “fully focus” on North American recycling activities. Clarios announced proposals on October 27 to acquire Ecobat’s three US critical mineral recovery and processing facilities, hinting at new investment in these sites and further potential expansion in the US. The looming sell-off of Ecobat’s North American business was exclusively revealed by Batteries International in October 2025. Now the sale to Clarios, financial details of which have not been disclosed, marks the final step in a portfolio transformation Ecobat started last year — under which the company has completed 10 divestitures spanning 17 sites across six countries in around 16 months, including the sale of its European operations. Ecobat president and CEO Tom Slabe said the deal “completes the strategic initiative we announced with the earlier sale of our European operations and delivers a strong outcome for Ecobat’s stakeholders”. The proposed acquisition will preserve and strengthen domestic critical mineral processing and recovery capacity at a time of growing demand for critical minerals and increasing focus on supply chain resilience, Clarios said. By integrating these facilities into its industry-leading circular supply network, Clarios said it will enhance its ability to recover, process and return valuable materials into the US manufacturing base. The proposed acquisition, conditionally expected to close by early calendar year 2027, includes Ecobat’s facilities in California, Indiana and Middletown, New York, as well as the Dallas office. Together, these facilities currently process more than 40 million batteries annually, recovering lead, tin, antimony and other materials. Clarios and Ecobat said they intend to work closely with employees, union representatives and regulators to focus on continuity of operations, environmental compliance, workforce stability and long-term investment in US critical mineral processing and recovery capacity. Clarios CEO Mark Wallace said: “As a world leader in critical minerals processing and recovery, Clarios is uniquely positioned to strengthen this highly capable US recycling operation supported by an experienced workforce. “We see a significant opportunity to build on Ecobat’s foundation by evaluating opportunities for future investment in these operations and supporting the continued success of the business.” The post Ecobat break-up complete as Clarios acquires North American recycling business appeared first on Batteries International .

title: Why Ford’s Included Inverter Matters for Bidirectional EV Power
content:
Charging
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
Ford's 2027 Fathom pairs a built-in inverter with bidirectional home power, signaling a more accessible path for EV energy integration.
October 28, 2026
3 Min Read
Ford Home Power Station and Ford Home Backup Power Panel.
Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and vehicle-to-home (V2H) technology has attracted growing attention as electric vehicles (EVs) become more closely connected to the grid. EVs are increasingly being viewed as mobile batteries that can store electricity and return it when needed. Automakers begin to present them as practical consumer features rather than long-term possibilities.
Ford’s news about the
2027 Fathom electric truck
fits into that trend. The company says the truck will start at $28,350 MSRP and offer available bidirectional AC power. The most notable element of the announcement is that the Fathom does not require a separate wall-mounted inverter to supply a projected 10 kW of AC power to a home. Instead, the vehicle includes the inverter.
The E-box is one of Fathom’s five main modules. It serves multiple functions including sending AC power to a home. Credit: Ford.
Why the integrated inverter matters
Including the inverter in the vehicle is a first. Extra hardware can make home energy integration more expensive, more difficult to install, and harder for buyers to understand. By integrating the inverter into the truck, Ford appears to be reducing one of the technical barriers that has limited wider appeal.
Related:
Five Takeaways on CATL's Heavy-Duty Truck Electrification Strategy
But Ford says customers who want to use these functions will still need the Ford Home Power Station, and those who want backup capability during outages will also need the Ford Home Backup Power Panel. Ford outlines two ways the system could work for customers:
The Home Power Management, which would allow owners to charge the truck when electricity prices are lower and use the vehicle’s stored energy to power the home when prices are higher. In locations with time-of-use electricity pricing, that model could help some households reduce monthly energy costs.
The Home Backup Power, which would allow the truck to send electricity to a home during an outage. That positions the vehicle as an alternative to traditional backup generators, with the added benefit of operating without natural gas or diesel.
For Fathom customers, that two-way flow of electricity can work in two ways. Credit: Ford.
Why this is relevant beyond one vehicle launch
This announcement reflects a broader shift in how EVs are being presented to consumers. EVs are no longer defined only by range, charging speed, or performance. Increasingly, they are also being marketed as part of a household energy strategy.
Bidirectional energy features have often been associated with higher-priced EVs, which can limit their relevance to mainstream buyers. A lower entry price, if maintained, suggests that these capabilities may begin to move into a broader section of the market. That could increase public awareness of bidirectional charging and raise expectations for future EV models.
Related:
Home EV Chargers Need NEC and UL-Listed 50-Amp EV-Certified Receptacles
At the same time, there are still open questions. The final installed cost will depend on the required hardware, home configuration, and installation work. The practical value of 10 kW of AC power will vary depending on household loads, and real-world backup duration will depend on how much battery capacity is available when an outage occurs.

title: The Tech Issue Making This Midterm Election Different
content:
Stationary Batteries
Along with the usual debates over funding for programs, transportation, and regulatory changes, this year's election cycle features a heated new flashpoint: whether AI data centers should be built — and where.
October 27, 2026
4 Min Read
Data centers have become a hotly-contested election issue in 2026, with citizens in many communities opposing their presence.
Nic Antaya / Stringer/ Getty Images News
With U.S. elections now less than a week away, candidates are making a final push for support in their costly campaigns. While local and state issues vary widely, one topic is drawing attention nationwide: whether, where, and how data centers should be built, and who will fund and power them.
The booming demand for AI infrastructure — driven in part by President Trump's
push to help the U.S. compete with China in artificial intelligence
— has created pent-up demand for new AI data centers across many states. But concerns over electricity usage, water consumption, and waste removal have led communities nationwide to push back against these projects. According to polls, attempts by data center operators to ease these concerns have largely been met with skepticism.
Gubernatorial races highlight the divide
Nowhere is the divide over data centers more apparent than in this year's gubernatorial races across several dozen states. A
MultiState
, a lobbying and government affairs organization, surveyed candidates in 36 gubernatorial races and found positions ranging from full support to conditional approval to temporary moratoriums.
Democratic candidates have generally favored moratoriums, while many Republican candidates have called for stricter regulation rather than outright bans. However, given politicians' often-shifting positions, some proposed measures have already drawn intense scrutiny from local advocacy groups.
New York: candidates take opposing stances
New York Governor Kathy Hochul, running for re-election against Republican Bruce Blakeman, was among the first to take a firm stance against data centers. In July, Hochul s
igned a one-year ban on large-scale AI data centers
. Business groups criticized the move as unilateral, arguing it could drive economic development away from the state — particularly in upstate regions already struggling with companies relocating elsewhere.
Blakeman has sharply criticized Hochul's approach, arguing
she should have worked with data center developers to address concerns
rather than impose an outright ban. Instead, he has called for operators to build their own electricity and water-recycling facilities to reduce strain on regional resources.
Blakeman's position echoes comments made earlier this year by President Trump, who s
uggested data center operators construct their own power-generation facilities
. One complication: power grid access is often regulated by state-run utilities, meaning operators would likely still need to negotiate arrangements with them.
Although Hochul's stance has been labeled draconian by critics, she appears to have public support. A
Siena Research Institute poll from Septembe
r found that 63% of New Yorkers surveyed would oppose data centers even after the one-year moratorium expires.
Texas: a Governor's changing position
Texas, a state with both a strong data center presence and ongoing power grid challenges, is also hosting a pivotal gubernatorial race. Governor Greg Abbott
has largely supported data center development
but recently called for state regulators to audit proposed projects before allowing them to connect to Texas's power grid. His position has since hardened further —
he's now calling for a halt on all new data center permits
until existing projects undergo a complete audit.
Abbott's opponent, State Representative Gina Hinojosa,
has called for a full moratorium on data centers
, according to an MSNBC report, and has advocated for new laws clarifying the scope of AI development. The same report cited a
Texas Politics Project poll
showing that 58% of Texas voters oppose data centers being built in their communities.
Ohio: over 200 data centers and a divided race
Ohio, reportedly home to more than 200 data centers, is also holding a closely watched gubernatorial election between candidates with starkly different views.
report on Cleveland.Com
says that Democratic candidate Dr. Amy Acton supports a conditional moratorium, stating she would back new data centers only if they meet requirements involving costs, labor, environmental safeguards, location and transparency.
The same report
noted that Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy favored projects only if they meet electricity-benefit, property-tax, and environmental conditions. Meanwhile, Libertarian candidate Don Kissick supports a temporary moratorium while the state assesses long-term effects and lawmakers establish standards.
Innovation Ohio, a progressive policy advocacy organization,
commented on the data center positions of Acton and Ramaswamy in a report
, stating that while Acton's proposal appears workable, Ramaswamy's plan offers little more than vague assurances.

title: ImportGenius: AI, Trade Intelligence and Supply Chain Risk
content:
ImportGenius: AI, Trade Intelligence and Supply Chain Risk
Prioritise Us
on Google
ImportGenius offers a source of customs and bill-of-lading information covering more than 25 countries, with data sourced from government customs agencies and other public trade records. Credit: ImportGenius
ImportGenius executives James Orr and Daniel Mikhail explain how AI, customs data and global supply chain visibility are reshaping trade intelligence
The pressures for supply chain leaders to identify potential supply chain risks, whether those are from
geopolitical
disruption or shifts in the competitiveness of individual suppliers, have never been greater than at present.
Data has become an increasingly important element of competitive advantage. But supply chain leaders understand that the strength of the data they are relying on to identify
disruption
, assess competitors and explain strategic decisions is a key variable.
ImportGenius is a supplier of international trade and supply chain intelligence. Through advanced data management technologies, the firm is able to help its clients make sense of hundreds of millions of shipping manifests and customs records from government agencies and private companies around the world.
Artificial intelligence
can be used to improve trade data quality, support supplier discovery, improve shipment analytics and sharpen supply chain mapping. However, the successful application of AI relies on its use as a support for human decision-making, rather than when it operates without controls.
AI moves beyond the chatbot
James Orr, Chief Product and Technology Officer at ImportGenius, says the company is applying AI across its data infrastructure rather than treating it solely as a conversational interface.
“The opportunity is not simply to put a chatbot on top of trade data. It is to use AI inside the data pipeline, where it can improve classification, correct anomalies and help customers work with information they can trust,” James adds.
ImportGenius describes its platform as a source of customs and bill-of-lading information covering more than 25 countries, with data sourced from government customs agencies and other public trade records.
The platform’s use cases include:
Competitor shipment monitoring to identify who companies buy from and sell to.
Supplier discovery based on shipment history, product descriptions and trade relationships.
Trade volume analysis using shipment counts, weight and estimated TEUs.
HS code enrichment for US maritime records that do not publish standard classifications.
Supply chain mapping across Tier 1, Tier 2 and further supplier relationships.
Tariff and country-of-origin analysis to assess exposure to changing trade conditions.
Lead generation based on importers, exporters, products and shipping lanes.
Multilingual trade-data search across datasets published in languages such as Spanish, Hindi and Russian.
Data governance is the foundation of AI
Orr stresses that trade data is inherently imperfect. Customs records may be supplied in different formats, languages and standards. Some information is entered manually, while other records may originate in scanned documents.
For enterprise users, this creates a governance challenge. A dataset can be faithfully reproduced from its source and still produce misleading results if errors are aggregated across millions of records.
ImportGenius said its data governance approach includes: data lineage, chain of custody, data quality monitoring, data preservation, transparent corrections and model confidence controls.
Orr gave an example involving US maritime data for the Port of Baltimore. A single declaration reportedly included an implausible weight of three trillion kilograms. When aggregated, the error suggested that Turkey represented 91% of trade through the port by weight.
The example illustrates why data quality matters. A single abnormal record may have little effect on a shipment search, but it can distort a market analysis, country comparison or supply chain forecast. The solution favoured by ImportGenius is to preserve both versions: the original source value and a corrected estimate designed for aggregate analysis.
Shipment data needs correction before analysis
One of the distinctions that James draws is between data cleansing and data imputation.
Data cleansing identifies and corrects errors in information already present. Data imputation adds a new value based on available signals, historical patterns and a defined model.
The company described several applications:
Weight correction: identifying values that are materially above or below a reasonable range.
TEU estimation: calculating twenty-foot equivalent units where volume information is incomplete.
Container-size validation: identifying impossible or inconsistent container descriptions.
Text parsing: extracting useful signals from unstructured shipment descriptions.
HS code imputation: predicting product classifications from descriptions and related evidence.
ImportGenius said its Lighthouse analytics environment contains approximately 170 million US maritime import records covering the previous decade. That scale makes manual review impractical and increases the importance of system-level modelling.
The TEU model must account for different cargo types, including: containerised cargo, less-than-container-load shipments, breakbulk cargo, grain and oil and inconsistent container-size descriptions.
The company said its estimates can also be compared with macroeconomic and government statistics, including data from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, to assess whether the aggregated picture is consistent with national trade activity.
AI adds HS codes to US maritime data
Harmonised System Codes classify traded goods internationally. The first six digits - HS6 - provide a globally standardised product classification, while additional digits may vary by country.
One complicating factor is that US maritime import and export records do not consistently publish HS codes. In order to circumvent this, ImportGenius has developed a machine-learning model to infer classifications from shipment descriptions and other signals.
The model uses a confidence-based approach. If an HS code appears directly in the product description, it can be extracted. Approximately 17% of relevant records contain an HS code directly in the product description, providing a particularly strong classification signal, according to ImportGenius. If the product description supports a specific classification, the model may assign an HS6 code.
Where a description supports a broad classification, the model may assign an HS2 or HS4 code.
However, there are cases where the description is ambiguous or unreadable, in which the record may remain unclassified. Finally, multiple HS codes may be returned where a shipment record contains several products.
The company’s public HS code materials state that its system combines a product-sanitising process with an AI classifier and applies an 80% or higher confidence threshold to displayed predictions.
The approach is most useful for aggregate analysis, such as comparing product categories across countries or suppliers. For highly specific searches, ImportGenius advises combining HS codes with keywords and other shipment fields.
Approximately 17% of relevant records contain an HS code directly in the product description, providing a particularly strong classification signal, according to ImportGenius.
Key uses for HS codes
Tariff assessment
Product searches
Customs compliance
Market analysis
Country-of-origin research
Import and export trend reporting
Global search connects trade datasets
Daniel Mikhail, Enterprise Sales Lead at ImportGenius, offers the example of a global search for coffee. The search combined product descriptions with HS code 0901, the 4-digit HS classification code for coffee.
The platform can use a single search to examine: product categories, HS codes, importers, exporters, countries of origin, shipping relationships, shipment volumes, date ranges and supplier networks.
Mikhail showed how analysts could use shipment data to understand whether goods are entering a market as one-off transactions or through consistent supply relationships.
The platform can reportedly present results by year, month, week or day, depending on the search and date range. Results can also be exported for further analysis in spreadsheets, customer relationship management systems or business intelligence tools.
Daniel Mikhail, Enterprise Sales Lead at ImportGenius, demonstrated a global search using coffee as an example. Credit: Daniel Mikhail/LinkedIn
Company profiling links shipments to business intelligence
ImportGenius introduced its Genius Company Profiler as a research tool combining web information with trade records. By accessing a company profile, clients can access information such as shipment history, company address, industry sectors, business model, value proposition, suppliers and countries of origin.
This meets the different needs of both supply chain professionals, who might need shipment intelligence to investigate a competitor, and sales professionals who need commercial research to identify active importers or potential customers.
The same workflow can support supplier vetting by showing a supplier’s customers, sourcing countries and apparent trade activity.
Key technology, data and ecosystem partners
1. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
Commissioner: Rodney S. Scott
Headquarters: Washington DC
US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is the largest federal law enforcement agency within the US Department of Homeland Security. CBP is the primary source for US maritime import and export data. The records are delivered digitally and updated daily. The data includes bill-of-lading information used to analyse shipment activity, importers, exporters, ports and cargo descriptions.
2. Bureau of Transportation Statistics
Director: Rolf Schmitt (acting)
Headquarters: Washington DC
The Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS), part of the US Department of Transportation (DOT), is the US agency responsible for compiling, analysing, and publishing statistics on commercial aviation, multimodal freight activity, and transportation economics. BTS data is a source for macroeconomic and transport-level data, which is used by ImportGenius to help identify anomalies in weight, volume and shipment calculations.

title: The Returns Value Gap: ReBound’s Circularity Concerns
content:
The Returns Value Gap: ReBound’s Circularity Concerns
Prioritise Us
on Google
ReBound explores how retailers can tackle the returns value gap. Credit: Getty
Though circularity is becoming more of a sustainability strategy, ReBound explores the returns value gap and how to protect operational margins
As customers are buying online more and more, the returns and recommerce markets are growing.
With this comes a particular challenge for retailers, as they need to find value from returned stock – can it be resold, can it be recycled, does it need to be written off?
ReBound is a global returns management specialist, helping brands as they simplify the returns process with increased efficiency, resilience and profitability.
Rising supply chain priorities
In September, ReBound Returns and Advanced Supply Chain conducted a study, revealing a major gap between
retailer’s circularity ambitions
and the value they are generating from returned items.
The Circularity Index was conducted using research from 150 senior leaders at mid-to-large UK and European retailers. The study found that 86% of retailers have a policy in place that focuses on
circularity in returns
, looking at resale, repair, refurbishment and recycling. Circularity is a core priority in returns management for 27% of leaders.
Despite this, there is a major gap when transforming these strategies into commercial value. Out of all returned items, as many as 12% generate no value, and only 9% of retailers resell more than half of their returned products at full price. Half of retailers state that between 6% and 40% of all returned items are written off, destroyed or discarded.
However, leaders are consistently looking for opportunities to unlock value, with 82% of retailers thinking that enhanced recommerce strategies could generate additional value for up to half of their returned stock. Though efforts are already being made to recover value from 62% of retailers, value recovery is lacking behind – but ReBound explores solutions in its Circularity Index.
At a glance
90% of customers say they would buy again after a positive return experience
1 in 3 customer purchases will end in a return
67% of shoppers explore the return policy before purchasing an item
12% of returned items generate no value
62% of retailers make efforts to recover value from goods that cannot be resold
ReBound Returns processes more than one million items every month
Closing the gap
Value recovery is a difficult task, with transport, processing and technology integration all proving to be an added cost. There are also challenges of whether the stock is returned in good condition or not, as well as the risk to brand reputation if quality is not maintained.
Disconnected data on condition, location, environmental impact and more means that the most effective option is often overlooked. Instead, it becomes a question of whether the item gets written off, rather than if time and resources are going to be spent extracting value from it.
end-to-end visibility and automation
, leading organisations are gaining more value from their returns. It is helping them plan a solution and measure compliance, delays and value much more efficiently.
Other leaders are building a recommerce ecosystem, with 98% of leading
retailers running an integrated strategy
. These include specialist partners for repair, refurbishment, donation and recycling.
“Collaboration comes up again and again,” explains Inge Baars, Head of Sustainability at ReBound.
Inge Baars, Head of Logistics at ReBound
“Not just because the challenges are too big for any one organisation to solve, but because we also need each other to keep the energy and motivation going.
“There’s still so much improvement needed, and sometimes simply staying hopeful and keeping the momentum matters.”
Out of the retailers, 28% have achieved a Leading circularity score, driven by consistency, speed and follow-through. These organisations have seen greater value recovery than their peers, demonstrating that the gap can be closed.
Returns are rising in today’s market, but the leading retailers are approaching these returns as an
opportunity for circular and profitable

title: Tesla’s rocket-shaped Robotaxi map in Houston is partly ‘fake’
content:
Tesla Robotaxi
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 8:18 am PT
Image: Tesla
Tesla’s new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won’t actually pick you up, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and former Tesla employee.
McKanna rode the service after Monday’s expansion and called Houston “by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area” he has seen. One trip quote had him spending about 40 minutes in a Robotaxi to go two blocks.
On Monday, Tesla
expanded its Houston Robotaxi geofence into the shape of a rocket
. It took the small launch zone in northwest Harris County and stretched it into a long corridor down to downtown and Bellaire, announced with “Houston, we have liftoff.”
McKanna runs Robotaxi Tracker, the crowdsourced site that tracks Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet and service areas, and he worked at Tesla this summer, so he knows the program better than most. He went to Houston to try it out. Here’s what he posted last night:
Another thing. Often AV service area maps advertised are kind of fake- they don’t actually go to everywhere in the polygon the provider publishes. Robotaxi Houston is probably by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area I’ve seen
I get they were doing it so they could get…
https://t.co/ILXIkmwGVp
The video shows the Robotaxi app with a pickup pin dropped in downtown Houston, well inside the polygon Tesla published. The app refuses it: “Location not available. Move the map to select a different location.”
McKanna acknowledged that AV service area maps are often “kind of fake,” since operators don’t serve every street inside the polygon they advertise. But he singled out Houston as the worst case he’s seen and said he understands Tesla did it “so they could get the starship shape,” which doesn’t seem like a good reason to fake availability.
About 40 minutes to go two blocks
The day before, he posted a trip quote that shows what this looks like for a rider:
40 min ride to cross 2 blocks downtown.
this is pretty rough
The app quoted a 2:05 pm pickup on the east side of downtown and a 2:48 pm drop-off at Houston Police Department headquarters on Travis Street, a couple of blocks away. Instead of cutting across downtown, the planned route runs south through Midtown and the Museum District to the Texas Medical Center area, then loops back north.
McKanna’s read is that the Robotaxi appears to be avoiding railroad crossings downtown, and he said it fits with “other strange routing in Houston.” He expects Tesla to fix it.
To be fair, he wasn’t down on the service overall. He wrote that, apart from that issue, it “feels really good in Houston,” with reasonable wait times and “significantly better driving than my recent Waymo rides.”
Waymo’s map isn’t perfect either
Tesla isn’t the only one. On Tuesday, Robotaxi Tracker reported that Waymo’s Orlando service area had shrunk by 10 square miles, down 8.4% to 109 square miles. McKanna explained what happened:
Someone accidentally added the airport 😭
Orlando’s airport was inside the map Waymo published, but McKanna checked the app and it won’t let riders set the airport as a drop-off yet. So the tracker took it out. Waymo’s airport service might be rolling out soon, and someone got ahead of the announcement.
That’s an airport on the edge of the map. In Houston, the dead zone is in the middle of downtown.
Electrek’s Take
First, a big thanks to Ethan. Tesla shares very little data about its Robotaxi program, and Robotaxi Tracker has become the best independent source on where Tesla’s fleet actually operates and how big it is. And as Orlando shows, he holds Waymo to the same standard.
Every AV operator has gaps in its map, Waymo included. But Waymo’s Orlando gap is an airport on the edge of the map that it’s likely about to add. Tesla’s Houston gap is downtown, and it drew a rocket first and figured out where the cars could actually go second.
Service and product should always outrank marketing, and that’s clearly not the case with Tesla’s Robotaxi. People rely on those maps to know if Tesla offers the service where they are. Faking the map just to make a rocket shape is completely stupid. Do better.

title: CATL pushes ahead with 20 Ah solid-state EV batteries, with 500 Wh/kg in sight
content:
Solid-state batteries
Peter Johnson
| Oct 28 2026 - 8:12 am PT
CATL hit another milestone in its
solid-state battery
development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027.
CATL continues advancing solid-state EV batteries
CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to
SNE Research
, CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026.
To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries.
When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027.
As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030.
Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries
have only reached
level four.
All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid.
Dr Wu Kai, CATL’s chief scientist (Source: CATL)
The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle.
CATL said its sulfide-based batteries have now entered 20 Ah trial production as it aims to achieve an energy density of 500 Wh/kg.
Trial production in 2027, reaching mass market in 2030
CATL’s 2027 timeline to begin small-scale production aligns with other automakers and battery manufacturers racing to introduce all-solid-state EV batteries.
Toyota, which has been promising solid-state batteries for nearly a decade now, aims to launch the
first all-solid-state battery-powered EV
in 2027 or 2028.
Toyota EV battery roadmap (Source: Toyota)
Using Sumitomo Metal Mining’s proprietary powder synthesis technology, Toyota claimed to have developed a “highly durable cathode material” for all-solid-state batteries last October. Toyota revealed
a prototype
last year, claiming it can deliver 745 miles (1,200 km) of range and charge in under 10 minutes.
However, like CATL, Toyota expects production to be limited and will not reach the mass market until closer to the end of the decade.
(Source: Toyota)
Samsung SDI, on the other hand, aims to begin mass production of its SolidStack all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027.
BYD, which ranks second in global EV battery sales behind CATL, also plans to launch its first solid-state battery-powered vehicle in 2027.
In an exclusive interview with
last month, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD is in “the leading position” on solid-state batteries and will “prove that” next year.
BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, aims to begin producing
sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries
in limited batches in 2027, ramping up to mass production by 2030.
Electrek’s Take
While solid-state batteries are often hailed the “holy grail” of battery tech, they are only one part of the equation.
CATL, BYD, and others continue advancing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion batteries, which will ultimately create more efficient, lower-cost options that offer various performance needs.
BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP batteries already deliver
over 1,000 km
(621 miles) of CLTC range. What’s next?
One thing is certain: New battery chemistries and evolving tech will only continue making EVs more efficient, unlocking longer driving ranges, faster charging speeds, and better performance.

title: Tesla confirms Vietnam entry to take on VinFast and its 36% market share
content:
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 7:28 am PT
Tesla has started hiring in Vietnam, and one of its recruiters says the company is now “officially coming” to the country. The five open roles include a sales manager, a service manager, and a charging project developer.
It’s a tough market to walk into. VinFast, the local all-electric automaker, has sold roughly 36% of every new car in Vietnam this year, more than its next five competitors combined.
Tesla quietly registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with about 77.7 billion dong (roughly $3 million) in charter capital and a business scope covering car imports, wholesale, and retail. Tesla never commented on it.
Now we have the first confirmation from someone inside the company. Ricky Ip, who recruits for Tesla,
posted on X
this morning:
Tesla is officially coming to Vietnam – and we're hiring.
Our mission is to build a world of amazing abundance and we are looking for passionate people to join us in Vietnam and help make that vision a reality.
Current Job Openings:
Sales Manager –
https://t.co/AvW3higssS
The five openings are Sales Manager, Service Manager, HR Business Partner, Purchasing Manager, and Project Developer, Charging. That last one is the tell. You don’t hire someone to develop charging projects unless you plan to build Superchargers in the country.
Tesla has followed this playbook before in Southeast Asia. It
went on a hiring spree in Thailand
in September 2022 and opened orders there three months later. It
started hiring in the Philippines
in September 2024 and launched in early 2025. So a Vietnam launch in the next few months wouldn’t be a surprise.
There’s no word yet on pricing, models, or store locations. Oddly, the recruiting graphic features the next-generation Roadster, with fine print saying the vehicle is “for illustration purposes only.” Fair enough.
VinFast owns Vietnam
Tesla isn’t walking into an empty market. It’s walking into VinFast’s backyard.
VinFast delivered 177,697 cars in Vietnam through the first nine months of 2026, out of a national total of about 495,000. That’s about 36% of the entire car market, gas cars included. In September alone, it had 37.7% of the market.
Here’s how the year-to-date numbers stack up against the next brands:
VinFast: 177,697
Toyota: 53,978
Hyundai: 35,412
Mitsubishi: 31,932
Ford: 30,353
Kia: 23,461
Add up Toyota, Hyundai, Mitsubishi, Ford, and Kia and you get 175,136. VinFast alone beat all five of them.
And it’s already passed its full-year 2025 volume with a quarter left to go. VinFast says September was its 25th straight month as Vietnam’s best-selling car brand.
The model mix tells you a lot about the market. The VinFast VF 3, a tiny two-door electric crossover that
launched at under $13,000
, is Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle so far this year. VinFast models held the top five spots in September.
The home-field advantages
VinFast builds its cars in Haiphong. Tesla would have to import everything, most likely from Giga Shanghai, and Vietnam kept passenger cars on its high-tariff list under the ASEAN-China free trade agreement.
Charging is another gap. VinFast’s sister company V-Green runs the country’s dominant charging network and announced plans this year to spend about $380 million on 99 ultra-fast charging stations. Third-party networks in Vietnam are still thin.
There is one thing working in Tesla’s favor. Vietnam just extended its registration fee exemption for battery-electric cars through the end of 2030, and that applies to imported EVs too.
And VinFast’s volume comes with an asterisk. A significant share of its deliveries go to GSM, the Xanh SM electric taxi and ride-hailing company founded by VinFast chairman Pham Nhat Vuong. VinFast has long relied on Vietnam for the bulk of its deliveries, which we pointed out when it

title: Ford casts 5,000 'unicastings' for Fathom EV truck in Tesla-style shift
content:
Ford Fathom
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 6:56 am PT
A Ford team member inspects a Fathom unicasting (Image: Ford)
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch.
Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.
Inside Ford’s unicasting process
The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford’s chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, in a
post on Ford’s From the Road blog
. The castings are made at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center and shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant for process testing and prototype builds. Louisville is the Kentucky factory Ford is retooling for the Fathom and other vehicles on its
Universal EV Platform
A Fathom unicasting at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center (Image: Ford)
Ford melts aluminum ingots at about 1,300°F (700°C) and injects the metal into either a front or rear structure mold. Once a robot pulls the part out, it goes into a quench tank, gets trimmed and machined, and then runs a gauntlet of checks: industrial X-ray scans for pores and voids, dimensional measurements in a climate-controlled room, optical surface scans, and lab tensile and chemistry tests on samples.
Machining a Fathom unicasting after it comes out of the casting machine (Image: Ford)
Nothing ships to Louisville until a batch clears every inspection. Ford says it’s also working on cutting cycle time and on designing the castings for “modular repairability.”
Every batch is held until it clears inspections, including industrial X-ray scans (Image: Ford)
That last part has been the main reason why automakers have been reticent about larger cast parts. Repair cost is the biggest knock on giant castings, since a damaged one-piece structure can turn a moderate crash into a write-off. Lucid executive Cory Steuben has said insurance concerns drove the company’s decision to skip gigacasting altogether.
Tesla started it with 70 parts
Tesla kicked this off in 2020 with the first IDRA Giga Press at Fremont, a machine with roughly 6,000 tons of clamping force. It
cast the Model Y’s rear underbody in a single piece
, replacing 70 parts, and Elon Musk said the change removed the need for about 300 robots.
Tesla wanted to go much further. It added a front casting, tied the two together with a structural battery pack, and moved to even bigger presses for the Cybertruck. But in 2024, Reuters reported that Tesla had backed away from its plan to cast nearly the entire underbody in one piece, and the automaker has reportedly since dropped the front casting on some Model Y production.
So Ford’s 146-to-2 figure looks great on paper. But it’s a front-and-rear layout, basically the same architecture Tesla launched with on the Model Y. Ford isn’t leapfrogging Tesla here. It’s catching up, just with a vehicle that will cost less than any Tesla on sale.
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 Fathom unicastings (Image: Ford)
The industry went bigger, but not everyone
Since that first Giga Press, a growing list of automakers have bought huge presses or committed to them:
Volvo started EX60 production at Torslanda this year with a single rear megacasting, and it
ordered two 9,000-ton-class IDRA presses
for its new plant in Slovakia.
Xiaomi runs 9,100-ton presses, combining 72 components into one underbody casting.
Xpeng casts the G6’s front and rear underbody, merging more than 300 parts across the two.
Honda is installing six 6,100-ton presses at its Anna Engine Plant in Ohio for EV components.
Toyota has shown its own gigacasting process, and group supplier Aisin plans to spend $3.4 billion over three years.
Others aren’t buying it. Stellantis has said it won’t invest in gigacasting, while BMW and Mercedes-Benz have stuck with smaller presses for body parts. Hyundai pushed its “Hypercasting” plan back two years.
Electrek’s Take
We’ve been tracking this casting race since Tesla’s first Giga Press showed up in Fremont, and the lesson so far is simple. Fewer parts is great, but the press alone doesn’t make a car cheap. The whole factory does.
That’s why Ford’s approach is worth watching. The unicastings are one piece of a bigger overhaul at Louisville, where Ford is splitting the line into three branches (front, rear, and the battery pack with the interior floor) that meet at the end. Ford says that can be up to 40% faster than its current assembly, or about 15% net once it reinvests some of the savings into automation and insourcing. It’s very close to the logic behind Tesla’s “unboxed” process, and they are betting it’s what actually gets you to a $28,350 truck.

title: New retro electric motorcycle to debut at EICMA with a novel feature: a second gear
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Oct 28 2026 - 6:48 am PT
Most electric motorcycles have something in common: a single-speed transmission. But a British company is preparing to shake things up at this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, where it will unveil a new electric motorcycle demonstrator featuring an unusual two-speed transmission designed to shift gears without interrupting power delivery.
The company behind the technology,
E-Motiv Shift Systems
, has developed what it calls a seamless powershift transmission, promising improved acceleration, better efficiency, and a more engaging riding experience.
Unlike conventional motorcycle transmissions, which generally require a brief interruption in power during gear changes, E-Motiv’s system is designed to maintain torque throughout the shift.
That could offer some interesting advantages for electric motorcycles, where a lower first gear could provide stronger acceleration while a taller second gear could help optimize motor efficiency at higher speeds.
Of course, most electric motorcycles don’t actually need multiple gears, and
very few have ever offered multi-speed transmissions
. Electric motors produce strong torque across a wide operating range, which is why manufacturers generally prefer the simplicity, lower weight, and reduced maintenance of single-speed drivetrains.
But that doesn’t mean a second gear couldn’t offer some benefits.
E-Motiv’s technology actually traces its roots back nearly 25 years to the Zeroshift transmission system, which eventually found its way into Aprilia’s MotoGP racing motorcycles in 2015.
The latest electric version was developed through a £1 million UK government-funded project involving motorcycle manufacturer BSA, the University of Bath, and the Institute of Advanced Automotive Propulsion Systems (IAAPS).
The demonstrator motorcycle, known as Demo 1, was conceived by British design consultancy Envisage and is being built by IAAPS. Real-world testing is scheduled to begin in early 2027.
E-Motiv will showcase the technology at EICMA from November 3-8, though the demonstrator remains a development project rather than a production-ready motorcycle.
Whether two-speed transmissions eventually become common on electric motorcycles remains to be seen. But if E-Motiv can deliver meaningful efficiency and performance improvements without adding too much weight, cost, or complexity, it could give future electric motorcycles another interesting trick up their sleeves.

title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours
content:
Tesla Semi
Electric Semi Truck
Fred Lambert
| Oct 28 2026 - 5:34 am PT
Photo: CHP Hayward
A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours.
The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.
What happened on I-880
The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. CHP Hayward then closed I-880 in both directions, citing “the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke,” and posted these photos from the scene:
🚨 TRAFFIC ALERT – I-880 FULL CLOSURE 🚨
A Tesla semi-truck has caught fire on I-880, resulting in a complete shutdown of both northbound and southbound lanes due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke.
The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they didn’t know why. No other vehicles were involved.
Northbound reopened Tuesday night. Southbound took much longer. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews beat that estimate, and
CHP Hayward posted
that all lanes were open at around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday.
The CHP photos show firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator hasn’t been identified, and Tesla, which doesn’t have a press office, hasn’t commented. The cause is under investigation.
The second Semi fire to close a California interstate
We’ve been here before. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi
caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap
while driving from Livermore to Tesla’s facility in Sparks, Nevada. At the time, no crash was reported. The
NTSB later found
the truck had left the road on a curve, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. Firefighters used about 50,000 gallons of water, and the lanes stayed closed for up to 15 hours.
Hayward is different. Without a crash, the focus shifts to the truck itself: the battery pack, the high-voltage system, the drive units, or something as ordinary as a tire or brake fire that spread.
And the timing isn’t great for Tesla. The company only
started volume production of the Semi in Nevada
this year, after nearly a decade of delays. WattEV ordered 370 Semis in May, mostly for drayage at the Port of Oakland, just a few miles up I-880 from where Tuesday’s truck burned. In September, Tesla was also named lead supplier on a 2,500-truck ZET SCALE order.
Electrek’s Take
First, some perspective, because this fire is going to get used as an anti-EV talking point. Truck fires are common. According to
NFPA data
, US fire departments responded to an average of 15,462 large-truck fires per year between 2018 and 2022. That’s about 42 a day, in a fleet that’s overwhelmingly diesel. Mechanical failure was a factor in 44% of them, and only about 2% were tied to a collision.
The same goes for cars. NFPA and DOT data put the US average at one vehicle fire for every 17 million miles traveled, and combustion vehicles make up the vast majority of that fleet. Tesla
one fire per 140 million miles for its own vehicles. That’s Tesla’s number, but independent data, like
government figures we’ve covered before
, points the same way: gas vehicles catch fire more often than EVs.
But that doesn’t get the Semi off the hook. Diesel fires happen across millions of trucks. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, but PepsiCo, its launch customer, was up to about 86 trucks in 2024, and volume production only started a few months ago. With a fleet that small, one fire with no crash is a big data point. It’s also the second Semi fire to shut down a California interstate in about two years.
So we need the cause. If a tire, a brake, or the trailer caught fire and it spread to the tractor, that’s a regular trucking problem. If the pack went into thermal runaway on its own, Tesla needs to find out why before tens of thousands of these trucks hit the road, and fire departments need a better plan than letting a loaded truck burn on a freeway for half the night.
The NTSB investigated the last one. It should look at this one too, and Tesla should publish what it finds. Will it?

title: Bosch’s popular e-bike motor just got upgraded with more power and less weight
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 28 2026 - 12:32 am PT
Bosch has unveiled the latest generation of its popular Active Line Plus electric bicycle motor, bringing more power, less weight, and a significantly smaller footprint to one of the company’s most widely used drive systems.
The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.
And while it isn’t
most powerful motor, the upgrades are fairly substantial.
The new Active Line Plus now produces up to 600 watts of peak power and 60 Nm of torque, along with a maximum pedal assistance level of 340%. That’s enough to give riders a healthy boost when accelerating away from traffic lights or climbing hills, without necessarily turning their everyday commuter into an overpowered mountain bike.
Like its predecessor, the motor is designed for Class 1 electric bicycles in the US, providing pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) without a throttle.
Remember, the Active Line motor is the drive system model that
many e-bike companies use for their modestly performing e-bikes
. It gives good power and control, combined with all the tech we’ve come to expect from Bosch, but it isn’t the motor e-bike makers use when they need an electric mountain bike to scale a steep mountainous trail.
Smaller, lighter, and quieter
Perhaps even more interesting than the increased power is what Bosch has done to the motor’s physical design.
The company developed a new two-stage gearbox that helps reduce the motor’s overall volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) off its weight.
The new drive unit now tips the scales at around 6 lb (2.7 kg), making it easier for bicycle manufacturers to integrate into slimmer, more traditional-looking frames.
Bosch also says the new gearbox uses specially machined gears to make the motor virtually silent, while updated sensors and software provide smoother, more natural-feeling pedal assistance.
That’s particularly important for a motor like the Active Line Plus, where riders are often looking for an experience that feels like riding a regular bicycle, just with a bit of extra help.
The motor also supports Bosch’s eShift electronic shifting system, which can automatically manage gear changes for riders who prefer to focus on pedaling instead of shifting.
Bosch has additionally improved the motor’s sealing and bearings for better all-weather durability. The housing uses approximately 40% recycled aluminum, helping reduce the carbon footprint of its production.
Coming soon to new electric bikes
Trek will be the first North American bicycle brand to introduce the new Active Line Plus motor, installing it on the company’s Marlin+ electric bike.
Bosch also announced several other additions to its e-bike ecosystem, including a new compact LED Controller that’s 65% smaller than its predecessor, an updated ConnectModule with Bluetooth-based theft tracking, and a new 720 Wh PowerTube battery weighing just 8.6 lb (3.9 kg).
There’s also a new Intuvia 200 display, offering a 2.4-inch grayscale screen for riders who prefer a traditional handlebar-mounted display.
While high-performance e-bike motors tend to grab the headlines with increasingly outrageous torque figures, there’s something to be said for improvements to the more practical end of the market – something for the riders looking for convenient and effective transportation instead of peak performance figures.
For the average commuter or recreational rider, a quieter, lighter motor with plenty of usable power is likely to make a bigger difference than squeezing another few dozen Newton-meters out of an already powerful drive system.
And with Bosch’s extensive network of bicycle manufacturing partners, we can expect to see this updated motor making its way into plenty of new electric bikes.

title: UK government approves nearly 2 GW of co-located solar in October - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Four projects in nationally significant infrastructure project planning pipeline granted planning permission by secretary of state. All four projects include battery energy storage systems.
Matthew Lynas
28 Oct 2026
Applications & Installations
Markets & Policy
Utility-scale
The 373 MW Cleve Hill Solar Park project was the largest UK PV plant when commissioned in summer 2025.
Four utility-scale projects have secured planning permission through the UK government’s pipeline for large infrastructure projects in October, including a co-located plant expected to have 1.12 GW DC installed solar capacity.
Great North Road Solar and Biodiversity Park and Frodsham Solar were both issued development consent orders (DCO) on Oct. 27, while Steeple Renewables Project and Green Hill Solar Farm were granted DCOs on Oct.9 and Oct. 8 respectively.
Developed by Elements Green, Great North Road Solar will be one of the largest in the United Kingdom when commissioned at its site northwest of Newark on Trent, England. The 1.12 GW project has secured a grid connection for import and export of 800 MW and will be built with a co-located 440 MW/880 MWh battery energy storage system.
Frodsham Solar is being developed by Cubico and project documents list the capacity as “around 150 MW”. The project near Chester, England, has a connection agreement with SP Energy Networks to supply up to 100 MW to the existing Frodsham substation.
Steeple Renewables Project in Nottinghamshire is being developed as a 450 MW solar generation project with approximately 150 MW of BESS in power output terms. The project is being developed by RES and is expected to use grid capacity made available from the decommissioning of the adjacent West Burton power station.
Green Hill Solar Farm is being developed by Island Green Power at a site north of Northampton. The project is expected to have a capacity of “up to 500 MW” and will also have a BESS installation.
All four projects were approved through the UK government’s Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project (NSIP) process, continuing a 100% success rate for solar in the NSIP pipeline. Run by the UK Planning Inspectorate, the NSIP process is used to approve or reject large-scale projects across industries – including solar projects in England with capacity greater than 100 MW. The first UK solar project approved through the NSIP process, the
376 MW Cleve Hill Solar Park,
was approved in 2020 and entered commercial operations in July 2025.

title: European solar startups raise €82 million in January-August - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Analysis by Avnet Silica says energy security remains the most significant driver of investment in European solar startups today as financing levels begin to increase after reaching an all-time low last year.
Patrick Jowett
28 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Highlights
Manufacturing
Venture capital investment in solar startups is stabilising in 2026 after dropping to a decade low last year, according to analysis by
Avnet Silica
A recent study by the electronics distributor found equity funding into the European solar sector reached €82 million ($91.2 million) by the end of August, compared to €24 million across the whole of 2025.
Harvey Wilson, Senior Manager Industrial Vertical Markets EMEA at Avnet Silica, told
pv magazine
that with a few additional deals closing in the last two months, total funding in 2026 could fall between €90-100 million by the year’s end.
While this year’s investments represent an upward trend, they remain off the pace of 2023, which recorded an all-time high of €285 million.
Wilson explained the surge in investment in European solar tech startups across 2022 and 2023 was most likely driven by energy security concerns, swiftly followed by a market correction through 2024 and 2025.
“The stabilisation we’re seeing in 2026 isn’t an indicator of a full market recovery just yet,” he said. “But it does show that while investors are being selective in a period of more expensive capital, they remain willing to invest when presented with the right opportunities.”
Additional analysis shared with
pv magazine
reveals PV recycling is the most funded market segment in 2026 so far, receiving €35 million, followed by lightweight PV modules (€16 million), residential PV systems with energy storage (€15 million), solar thermal technologies (€10.3 million) and space-based solar (€5 million).
Avnet Silica’s analysis adds 93% of the €82 million invested by the end of August went to early-stage companies. There were five deals over €10 million in the first eight months of the year, which represented the joint highest year on record for large early-stage transactions.
The median funding round across all stages of European solar startups this year stands at €15 million, which Avnet Silica says is the highest its been in over 15 years. The company’s research says this is a result of venture capitalists focusing on a small number of substantial investments rather than spreading their bets across the sector.
Avnet Silica explains that investors have “largely retreated from the extremes of the investment spectrum”, avoiding both unproven seed concepts and heavy capital demands of late-stage growth, and are instead focusing their capital on “select early-stage opportunities that offer a balance of validated technology and upside potential”.
Wilson told
pv magazine
the most significant driver of investment in European startups today remains energy security, but also pointed towards ensuring the security and privacy of the hardware, supply chain and the data being transmitted.
He said technology providers in Europe need to be actively adapting to regulations including the EU Cyber Resilience Act and Net-Zero Industry Act if they want to remain viable within the regulated supply chain.
“If European startups can position themselves as a solution to these security and compliance challenges, investors have shown they’re willing to back the right opportunity, and this new regulatory landscape could help close the deal,” Wilson added.

title: Acid-free molten salt method recovers 94% of silver from solar cells - pv magazine Global
content: Researchers in China have developed an acid-free method to recover silver wires from end-of-life aluminum back-surface-field solar cells using a molten mixture of sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide (NaOH-KOH). The molten salt etches the cell’s silicon nitride (SiNx) passivation layer and weakens the bond between the silver and the SiNx, allowing the silver wires to detach and be recovered directly as metal, rather than being dissolved into silver ions and recovered later. At 230 C for 150 seconds, the process recovered 94.34% of the silver and effectively removed the SiNx layer, the researchers said. Maximum silver recovery reached 97.11%. Silicon substrate loss was limited to 2.62% at 230 C for 100 seconds. The researchers found that once the SiNx layer is removed, the exposed silicon is attacked by hydroxide ions in the molten salt, causing pitting and converting silicon into soluble sodium and potassium silicates. The work builds on an earlier NaOH-KOH molten salt recycling approach reported in 2024. The researchers said existing molten salt methods avoid acids but do not effectively control silicon substrate loss, and that the new study clarifies the mechanisms behind both silver recovery and silicon loss. Most silver recovery from end-of-life modules still relies on acid leaching with nitric acid and other strong acids, which converts silver into ions and generates nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions and acidic wastewater, according to the researchers. They noted that silver accounts for less than 0.03% of the weight of an end-of-life module but nearly half of its total value, and that the first generation of commercial PV modules is now reaching the end of its 25- to 30-year life. The work was carried out at laboratory scale. The findings appear in “ Sustainable recovery of silver wires from crystalline silicon solar cells ,” which was recently published in the Journal of Cleaner Production. Researchers from Australia’s University of Newcastle, CSIRO Energy and PV Industries recently recovered an average of 93% of silver electrochemically from a simulated nitric acid leaching solution using stainless steel cathodes. Separately, researchers from the University of New South Wales, Gdansk University of Technology and the Polish Academy of Sciences found that silver can make up to 47% of a module’s recoverable value , though falling silver content in newer panels will lower future recycling revenue. The government of Togo is asking stakeholders to comment on documents covering the development of a large-scale solar project ahead of issuing a competitive tender.

title: New flywheel design could eliminate power converter for grid connection - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
A research team has built a fixed-speed flywheel prototype that uses a wire-rope mechanism to move weights inward and outward during discharge and charge. The system briefly supplied power to the electrical supply, but steady-state losses prevented net electrical energy discharge over the complete operation.
Lior Kahana
28 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Batteries
Energy Storage
System Integration
Clockwise from left: the experimental setup, the flywheel in its open state, and the flywheel in its closed state
A research team at
Tokyo University of Science
in Japan has developed and tested a prototype fixed-speed flywheel energy storage system (FESS). Flywheels store energy as rotational motion and suit short-duration applications that require rapid charging and discharging, such as grid frequency regulation. Conventional systems use a power electronic converter to vary the flywheel’s speed while exchanging electricity with the grid. The proposed system moves weights within the flywheel instead of changing its speed, potentially eliminating the converter and reducing costs.
“The main novelty is the development and experimental evaluation of a flywheel mechanism that enables charging and discharging through active changes in its moment of inertia while maintaining an approximately constant rotational speed,” corresponding author Ryoga Sugata told
pv magazine
. “To our knowledge, experimental studies of such mechanisms remain limited, particularly those that deliberately reduce the moment of inertia to extract stored rotational energy.”
The researcher added that his team developed the design to address losses in their earlier winch- and ball-screw-based mechanisms. “A potential future application is to add controllable active-power storage capability to synchronous condensers. Our longer-term objective is to investigate whether a synchronous condenser can combine its usual reactive-power and inertial support with fast, controllable active-power exchange enabled by the variable-inertia flywheel,” he added.
To test the concept, the researchers built a prototype using a modified centrifugal brake as the flywheel, with two 0.856 kg weights attached to pivoting arms. They added wire ropes, pulleys, bobbins, gears, an electromagnetic clutch, and a brake to control the weights’ position. A shaft connected the flywheel to a 0.75 kW, three-phase induction machine that acted as both a motor and a generator.
The team tested charging and discharging at synchronous speeds of 400, 450, and 500 rpm using a regenerative variable-frequency power supply, with voltage and frequency held constant during each test. For charging, they released the clutch, allowing centrifugal force to move the weights outward. For discharging, they activated the brake to drive the reeling mechanism and pull the weights inward.
They measured voltage, current, shaft torque, rotational speed, and clutch and brake voltages, and calculated electrical and mechanical power and energy. They then compared the results with theoretical values, subtracting steady-state power consumption to isolate the energy associated with moving the weights. The analysis excluded the energy consumed by the clutch, brake, and control circuitry.
“The most surprising finding was that charging and discharging efficiencies showed different trends as rotational speed increased,” Sugata said. “Over the tested range of 400–500 rpm, charging efficiency decreased slightly, whereas discharging efficiency increased. For example, after subtracting the steady-state mechanical power input, mechanical charging efficiency decreased from approximately 51% to 49%, while mechanical discharging efficiency increased from approximately 40% to 53%.”
The team attributed the difference to the distinct loss characteristics of the two operations, the academic said. During charging, frictional losses increase with centrifugal force, limiting the benefit of higher speeds. During discharging, the main losses appear to increase more slowly than the available stored energy, reducing their relative impact. The researchers said that improving efficiency would require addressing the specific loss mechanisms of both operations.
More according to the results, at 500 rpm, the researchers calculated a theoretical storage capacity of 36.61 J. After subtracting steady-state power consumption, the prototype consumed 84.1 J during charging and discharged 16.4 J, corresponding to electrical efficiencies of 43.3% and 45.1%, respectively.
“We demonstrated electrical power delivery to the grid without a power electronic interface for frequency conversion, although steady-state losses still prevented net electrical energy discharge over the complete discharge operation,” Sugata added. “In follow-up research, we plan to improve the mechanical design to reduce friction and losses associated with clutch and brake operation. We also plan to investigate replacing the induction machine with a synchronous machine and evaluate the effects on electrical losses and charging and discharging performance.”
The article “
Charging and discharging performance of a fixed-speed flywheel energy storage system with a reeling-type inertia control mechanism
” has appeared in the
Journal of Energy Storage.

title: Sunkean advances copper-to-aluminum jumpers for PV DC systems - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The manufacturer has developed a copper-to-aluminum jumper solution for PV DC-side applications, addressing conductor material costs, field installation efficiency, and the long-term reliability of copper-to-aluminum connections in utility-scale solar projects.
Sunkean Cable
28 Oct 2026
Technology & Products
Utility-scale
For utility-scale PV plants, DC-side cabling often spans considerable distances, making conductor selection an important factor in overall material costs. SUNKEAN’s copper-to-aluminum jumper solution uses a dedicated transition structure that allows aluminum conductors to be used in selected sections of the DC-side circuit, reducing copper consumption while maintaining the required connection performance. Project experience indicates that, under suitable application conditions, the copper-to-aluminum approach can deliver cost savings of nearly 50%. For cable runs exceeding 20 meters, the economic advantage of aluminum becomes increasingly significant.
Installation efficiency is another consideration behind the jumper design. SUNKEAN supplies the copper-to-aluminum jumper as a pre-assembled cable harness, with the copper-to-aluminum connector assembled before delivery. At the project site, installers only need to crimp the copper connector to the copper cable, eliminating the need for complex copper-to-aluminum conversion work in the field. For utility-scale projects involving large numbers of repeated DC connections, this prefabricated approach can reduce field operations and improve installation consistency.
The copper-to-aluminum connector is central to the solution. The challenge in adopting copper and aluminum conductors is not simply replacing one material with another but ensuring a stable connection between dissimilar metals over the operating life of the system. SUNKEAN’s copper-to-aluminum terminals use solid-state friction welding, in which heat generated by high-speed friction, combined with applied pressure, creates a solid-state bond between copper and aluminum without melting the materials.
Compared with conventional fusion welding, the process avoids key manufacturing challenges associated with the different melting points and thermal expansion characteristics of copper and aluminum. The terminals also feature a high-performance multilayer protective coating to enhance environmental resistance at the connection interface and reduce the impact of moisture, heat, salt spray, and other environmental factors. Contact resistance is controlled at ≤0.3 mΩ, with current ratings of 46 A, 55 A, 70 A, and 95 A available for different applications.
As utility-scale PV projects continue to focus on reducing BOS (Balance of System) costs and improving construction efficiency, copper-to-aluminum conversion is emerging as an option for optimizing conductor materials on the DC side. SUNKEAN’s copper-to-aluminum jumper applies this approach through a prefabricated DC-side harness, offering a way for PV projects to reduce copper consumption while simplifying field installation.

title: Qvantum launches 50 kW propane heat pump for residential, commercial applications - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The Swedish heat pump manufacturer said its the QA50 heat pump delivers a maximum heating capacity of 50 kW and a COP of up to 3.12. The system uses propane (R290) as a refrigerant, operates at outdoor temperatures ranging from -25 C to 43 C, and can be integrated into low-temperature ambient heat networks.
Emiliano Bellini
28 Oct 2026
Technology & Products
Commercial & industrial
Heat pumps
Residential
The QA50 heat pump system
Swedish heat pump manufacturer
has launched a new air-to-water heat pump designed for multi-residential developments and light commercial buildings.
“With a wide operating window, the QA50 is ideal as the primary energy source for low-temperature ambient loop systems. Its compact dimensions and modular design allow multiple units to be combined, creating a scalable solution that can be tailored to project requirements while maximising available plant room space,” the company said in a statement.
The new unit measures 1,195 mm × 980 mm × 1,900 mm and weighs 363 kg. It can reportedly operate at outdoor temperatures ranging from -25 C to 43 C.
According to the manufacturer’s technical datasheet, the QA50 delivers a maximum heating capacity of up to 50 kW and a coefficient of performance (COP) of up to 3.12. Its seasonal coefficient of performance (SCOP) reaches 4.52 at 35 C and 3.26 at 55 C, corresponding to A+++ and A++ energy efficiency ratings, respectively. The unit has a rated heating output of 25.56 kW at 35 C and 25.53 kW at 55 C. It offers a maximum heating-water flow temperature of 70 C, a cooling capacity of 51.93 kW at A35/W25 and a heating capacity of 30.3 kW at A-10/W55.
The heat pump features two refrigerant circuits containing 1.5 kg of propane (R290) each, for a total refrigerant charge of 3 kg. It has a maximum electrical input of 24 kW, a maximum operating current of 30 A and a three-phase electrical supply of 380 V to 415 V. The unit has an IPX4 protection rating and its declared sound power level is 75 dB(A), while its sound pressure level at a distance of 1 m is 70 dB(A).
The heat pump’s modular design allows multiple units to be connected in cascade configurations to meet higher heating and cooling demands. It can be integrated with existing building energy infrastructure and supports communication with building management systems via Modbus.
Qvantum said the QA50 has been developed primarily for use in fifth-generation district heating and cooling networks, also known as ambient heat networks, which typically operate at temperatures between 10 C and 30 C.
In these applications, the QA50 can be combined with the company’s QG water-to-water apartment heat pump to provide space heating, domestic hot water and cooling at the individual apartment level. The low-temperature network configuration is designed to reduce distribution heat losses compared with conventional high-temperature heating networks.
The QA50 can also operate as a standalone heating and cooling solution for offices, leisure facilities and mixed-use buildings.
The system incorporates Qvantum’s QC PRO controller, which enables centralised management of multiple heat pumps and associated heating and cooling components. Other features include remote monitoring and diagnostics through the company’s Q Service platform, over-the-air software updates and compatibility with flexible electricity tariffs.
